This is more flattening momentum than I allowed for in my previous flat call with low conviction (0.32). The slope is now at its 12-month low (0.47pp), suggesting this is not mean reversion noise but a structural drift. Over 21 days, the slope fell 15bp; over 63 days, it fell 6bp; over a year, it fell 65bp. The trajectory is unambiguously downward.

The mechanism matters: the 10-year has dropped 13bp over 21 days while the 2-year rose 2bp. This is front-end stability with long-end weakness—the classic signature of flattening driven by falling long-dated yields, not front-end repricing. Over 63 days, both legs moved up (2-year +38bp, 10-year +32bp), but the 2-year's faster rise still compressed the spread by 6bp. Current absolute levels are 2.27% (2y) and 2.74% (10y), so the 10-year is not elevated in a way that looks vulnerable to more compression on valuation grounds—but the momentum is against steepening.

The 10s30s slope at 0.23pp is shallow, offering no support for a steeper bull bear steepening trade on the long end. Policy language remains accommodative and forward-guidance-anchored; there is no hawkish shock visible in the language.

My prior view was that the slope would remain flat because the evidence was mixed. It is no longer mixed. The slope has fallen to its range low and momentum is clearly downward. I misread the 21-day compression and should not have rated that a lean-flat call. This warrants a clear down signal, though not maximum conviction because one month ahead, near the range low with near-zero distance from flat, there is some reversion risk embedded in the measurement itself.
